messages:
Maria V.: Hey folks — opened a PR to consolidate the Dedicated Capacity onboarding & SLO section. PTAL: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/482
Ajay K.: quick skim — SLO table still lists 99.9% for eviction window but our SLA matrix says 99.5 for burst tiers. which do we want in docs?
Maria V.: good catch. I pulled 99.9 from the Dedicated contract example draft; we should standardize to the public SLA numbers (99.5 for burst). I'll update table if we agree.
Olivia T.: also the SDK snippet in the "configure autoscale" step is missing the `region` param, caused one customer confusion yesterday. snippet currently: ```python client.create_capacity(name="team-a", gpus=8, autoscale=True)``` should be: ```python client.create_capacity(name="team-a", gpus=8, autoscale=True, region="us-west-2")```
Kevin L.: nit: add example using `scale_policy=conservative` and an inline comment about cost vs latency. many readers assume autoscale==aggressive.
Tom B.: happy to take the autoscale examples and add a Terraform equivalent. can someone paste the minimal TF snippet we recommend?
Maria V.: @Tom B. putting draft TF snippet below — please adapt and add comments: ```hcl resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "prod" { name = "prod-pool" gpus = 16 region = "us-west-2" autoscale { enabled = true min_replicas = 1 max_replicas = 8 policy = "conservative" } }```
Ajay K.: Couple link fixes: the migration guide anchor `#isolation-models` 404s (migrates.md). also the sample rollout policy link points at an internal google doc; we need a public snippet.
Olivia T.: I'll add an inline migration checklist: account prep, VPC peering, KMS key setup, reserved capacity sizing. Short bullets should help first-time infra folks.
Maria V.: docs-bot ran the link checker and flagged 3 broken links — list posted in the PR comments.
docs-bot: Link check report: 3 broken links found — files/migrates.md#isolation-models, examples/terraform/dedicated-legacy.md, internal/rollout-policy.gdoc.
Kevin L.: For SLO language: can we add an example SLA table per tier (standard, burst, reserved)? I can draft a compact table with numeric targets + what triggers escalation.
Tom B.: done a quick pass on TF comments — pushed a small commit to the branch with variableization for `region` and `pool_size`.
Maria V.: status update: I'm going to: (1) change visible SLA to 99.5 for burst, (2) add the SDK `region` param and conservative policy example, (3) include TF snippet and link to a public rollout example. Will ping again when ready for final review.
Ajay K.: lgtm, please add a short blurb on isolation: what workloads get colocated vs pinned-GPU. customers ask that a lot.
Olivia T.: added the migration checklist to the PR body with KMS/K8s note.
release-bot: Reminder: docs freeze window starts in 48h for the platform release on 2026-03-23. Plan accordingly.
Maria V.: thanks @release-bot — will aim to merge before freeze. tagging @Tom B. for final TF review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Tom B.: will review first thing and then we can ship.
Maria V.: thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround.
